claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the game features a praised story, characters, and atmosphere alongside criticism of repetitive missions or open-world design.

citations.review_text:
GTA IV has strong narrative and character work — that’s clearly the talent of the original Rockstar team. Niko’s story and the supporting cast are well done.
I’ve got full GTA fatigue at this point though, and I could care less. The open-world formula just doesn’t do much for me anymore, even when the writing is solid.

GTA IV is not a game everyone will understand, and honestly, not everyone can appreciate its beauty.

Some people play GTA for chaos, explosions, and endless fun. But GTA IV is different. It's about loneliness, friendship, betrayal, sacrifice, and the dark reality of life.

Liberty City isn't just a map; it's a world with its own atmosphere, stories, and feelings. Niko Bellic isn't just another GTA protagonist. He's a man trying to escape his past while struggling to build a better future.

However, GTA IV isn't perfect.

The driving physics can be frustrating, especially if you're used to the smoother driving in other GTA games. Cars feel heavy, turning takes some getting used to, and some missions can become annoying because of the driving.

Performance is another major downside. Even on modern PCs, the game can have optimization issues, stutters, and occasional technical problems. Some missions also feel repetitive, and the lack of certain activities compared to GTA V can make the open world feel limited.

But despite all these flaws, GTA IV has something special.

The atmosphere, the story, the characters, the soundtrack, and even the rainy streets of Liberty City create an experience that is difficult to forget.

GTA IV may not be perfect, but it has a soul that many modern games struggle to capture.

Not everyone understands GTA IV. Not everyone sees its beauty. And that's okay.

Some games are meant to be played. GTA IV is meant to be felt.

**10/10 for its soul, story, and atmosphere.**

citations.review_text: It's still my favorite GTA, but it needs some love from rockstar. Lot's of issues with crashing and missions not loading.

Only reason this is a negative review is due to many lacking features and the fact that you have to install FusionFix, DXVK, and Various Fixes just to get good performance and fix the copius amount of bugs.

Plus the game is missing MID MISSION CHECKPOINTS for when you run into issues stemming from crappy controls or one of the other many things that could go wrong in a mission, there is no quit to menu button which isn't super important but it is just a basic feature they could have easily coded into the pc port.

Finally for the good part of the game, the main story was great, i haven't played the dlcs yet but if they are as good as i have heard then i can look past the bugs and issues to play them, if you haven't played this game yet wait for a sale and ensure you install the 3 things i mentioned at the start of the review as they are VERY necessary to ensure you can enjoy the game.

Buy this game at your own risk. For a 5 billion dollar company that is always weaving "legacy" into their storylines... You will have to fix this game yourself with mods. And even after that, your progress will be halted constantly. I lost track how many times I had to rewind an hour and a half on the clock because my game crashed. Grand Theft Auto IV comes very close to being a masterpiece. The original hype, launch, and respect it still commands all these years later prove that. From the gritty and grounded story to the well written characters, the satirical humor and parodies that balance out the dark and gloomy atmosphere, the relatable protagonist you play, and the sheer amount of things you can do in Liberty City. Everything clicks together brilliantly.

While the sequel GTA V is great and obviously looks newer, GTA IV actually beats it in several key areas that make it worth playing. The gritty atmosphere and heavier driving physics complement the tight roads of Liberty City, encouraging a very engaging driving experience. On top of that, the Euphoria ragdoll mechanics and the way NPCs react to both the world and Niko make the city feel genuinely alive in a way that makes you forget about its aged graphics. Looks really good though with the FusionFix mod I talk about below.

Important Note for PC: The PC port is not well made and barely works. Download and install FusionFix before you start. It’s a simple drag-and-drop mod that fixes performance issues, restores missing console edition visual effects and graphics, and makes the game run the way it was always meant to. Once that's installed, this is easily one of the best open world experiences ever made.

*Played with Fusion Fix*
This is a phenomenal game. 4 is a 8.5, Lost and the Damned is a 6.5 and The Ballad of Gay Tony is a 9.
Fusion fix is the way to play these titles on pc. Easy top install and makes it play and run like a dream. 4 and TBoGT are must play titles in the GTA franchise with TboGT arguably having the best vibes and missions out of the franchise. It aint San Andreas level but even with 5.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the vehicle handling as heavy and floaty, noting that it has a steep learning curve.

citations.review_text: The best GTA story of all GTAs series so far. The part has the best driving physics as well as very deep plot that makes a player to choose between a deal or revenge options while each choice has its own consequence. The part is over 15 Y.O and It still feels relevant.

GTA IV is excellent and still worth a playthrough nowadays (although I applied fusionfix).  I grew to really enjoy the car handling which feels super floaty in the beginning and it feels easy to crash and wipe out, but as you play more and more you get really good at driving and it feels amazing tearing down the road in a Ferrari knowing that a player less skilled wouldn't be able to adjust the inches needed to avoid a total collision.  It has all the excellent things that GTA brings - that moment the right song hits during a thunder storm in the city and it's just perfect, the dialogue where the content is dumb juvenile jokes but presented in an intelligent way, and expansive social/action simulator.

Lost and Damned is okay - it's not great.  The story is a bit off - it's about biker gangs and what you see is what you get instead of Rockstar's usual ability to create surprise and layers with characters.  Ballad of Gay Tony is excellent and corrects issues with the first DLC.  It's about being the enforcer of a rich gay club owner drowning in debt.  The action is better, the characters are more interesting, and it just feels more well rounded.  The DLCS are worth going through especially Ballad of Gay Tony.

There are a couple of frustrating issues.  The controls for flying the helicopter are dumb - you have to use the numpad for part of it and its tough to control and a helicopter's movement is naturally unintuitive, and there are missions where you have to use a helicopter's guns, but you can only fire in a straight line which means you have to maintain your height with one hand, the other control tilting, and when you have a brief half second where things line up you quickly try to shoot - it's frustrating.  The other thing is the penalty for dying.  If you fail a mission you lose your armor and pay a hefty fee to the hospital, which suck but relatively fair punishments.  However, you also lose all ammunition that you used during your attempt - this is worse tha…

It's a great game. It's fun as fk to drive. Don't listen to anyone who says otherwise. It takes something called a learning curve, something the complainers don't understand. Fortunately, everything else, such as the gameplay and missions, is fun. The problem is there are a lot of glitches. In fact, I'd recommend just buying a 360 or PS3 to play this shit because Rockstar hates it,  FusionFix (which is the only application that made this shit playable) won't save you if you're playing after 11/13/2026. Just know that you will experience loading issues due to the recent Rockstar update. There are answers in the discussions, which, if you're looking, you'll see multiple more. Would I recommend this game? Hell yeah, 100%. On PC? Fuhuhug no. Play it on original hardware. Rockstar grapes you.

I liked this game, at the beginning, it was a bit harder for me to get into because the atmosphere was so dark. The city itself felt dark and looked quite depressing. But over time, as I progressed through the missions, the atmosphere started to feel lighter, and damn, the city really started to look so good.

I really loved the story, it was just so damn great, it mixed serious moments with Rockstar's usual humour really well.

The driving system, well, this is where I know people's opinions differ. Some like it, some don't. I'm gonna say that personally, I didn't enjoy it that much. At first, it was a bit tricky to get used to, and after playing for a while, I got the hang of it, but I'm still definitely not the biggest fan.

Even though the game is quite old, it still holds up surprisingly well. It has its flaws, of course, but the story, atmosphere and overall experience make up for them.

I definitely recommend this game. It has great characters and and an absolutely amazing story.

I come back to this title every couple years as it is hands down the best story in the GTA franchise. It trades the flair of the other titles and does away with it, opting for a more gritty realism extending into vehicles and their mechanics.

Unfortunately, they trade away a bit too much of what made other games fun. There is no real reason that you cannot modify your vehicles or buy a garage/additional properties for vehicle storage and the world feels maybe a bit lacking in content since there is literally no reason to visit many portions of the map, but that is part of the realism in my opinion.

The good: Story (so much so that I keep forgetting how bad the ending sequence is), characters, world design
The bad: customization options, vehicle storage, unclear/useless instructions(sometimes it tells you to use stealth or a certain approach, only make that the worst possible thing to attempt)
The neutral: car realism(I love the stalling, the hit zones, etc, but I can see how it would bum someone else out), lack of monetary value (money is kind of worthless in this title)

The game is old, but well worth the full price, but is also on sale often enough that it's just worth playing. You should definitely unlock the graphics if you decide to play it though. Otherwise, it's visually rough at best on newer PCs.

Despite all the technical problems, I keep coming back to GTA IV. I've played it three times, experienced both expansions, and Niko's story still stays with me.

It's an old game, yet there still aren't many games that deliver this combination of storytelling, character writing, atmosphere, and physics. It has flaws, but it also has something that makes it unforgettable.

GTA IV is not a perfect game. Its PC port is a mess, some mechanics have aged, and certain features are noticeably absent.

But the story? The characters? The atmosphere? Absolutely incredible.

My recommendation: YES.

If you're a GTA fan, play it. Experience Niko's story, play both expansions, and give the driving physics some time before throwing your keyboard out the window.

Just be prepared to fight a few technical battles before you can enjoy the actual game.

A masterpiece deserves a better PC port.

citation.review_text:
I've nostalgia maxxed with GTA VC, SA and V, but somehow, despite completing this back in 2018, I only remember and reminisce about certain parts of it, like the atmosphere of Liberty City, Roman's bowling line, Lil Jacob's Caribbean accent, the banger theme music and how brilliant the ending(s) were. I've come to the realisation that certain things you forget to reminisce about hit harder when the deja vu kicks in and you finally remember and rediscover those forgotten fragments. And then you get miserable about how much you miss the time period when you first encountered this piece of faded, distant memory that you didn't even realise you'd forgotten. It's not necessarily nostalgia for the game itself (tho it is partly that). Sometimes it's nostalgia for the person you were when you first encountered it.

GTA 4 is something along those lines for me. I feel like I'm pretty familiar with both versions of the Los Santos map and Vice City, but Liberty City, for some reason, feels quite enigmatic despite having played two games that feature it. Getting reminded of the UI audio, GPS sounds and voices that I'd completely forgotten about, but which at one point were practically spammed into my ears, felt oddly satisfying. The GPS itself is pretty slow and inaccurate a lot of the time. For some reason I've always felt that 4 is the niche indie darling in the franchise compared to juggernauts like V, VC and SA. Would barely come across people who played 4 but would've played or atleast heard of the other games.

GTA 4 has a smaller map than SA and less mission variety, but it still passed the vibe check for me. After playing all three in quick succession, though, I feel like SA has the best variety of missions, even if some of them can be pretty challenging and act as roadblocks to finishing the game, followed by GTA V with its heists (there should've been more of those, tbh). single_points.text: One reviewer says the optimization was terrible, and they ran into so many issues with infinite loading screens and cutscenes that simply refused to load.

citation.review_text:
Finally done with the entire GTA IV series!

What an unforgettable experience. After finishing the classic GTA trilogy, GTA IV really left a special impression on me. For a game released back in 2008, it's honestly insane how much content it has to offer, which is both a blessing and a curse for someone going for 100% completion.

The main story was great and everything ran pretty smoothly, same goes for The Lost and Damned DLC. However, The Ballad of Gay Tony was a completely different story. The optimization was terrible, and I ran into so many issues with infinite loading screens and cutscenes that simply refused to load. I probably spent more time trying to fix those issues than I'd like to admit.

Overall, GTA IV probably has the best story in the entire GTA franchise, and it's definitely an experience I'll remember for a long time.

And of course, Niko the Serbian absolutely carried the whole thing.
